newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Too early for normal Jordan-Kuwait ties - Kuwait.
newsitem.headline: Too early for normal Jordan-Kuwait ties - Kuwait.

text.p: Kuwait said on Thursday it was too early to discuss normalising ties with Jordan, a fellow Arab state accused of backing Iraq during its 1990-91 occupation of the Gulf state.
Prime ministers of Kuwait and Jordan exchanged congratulatory messages recently but the official Kuwait News Agency (KUNA), quoting an official source, said they did not touch on bilateral relations.
"Concerning upgrading diplomatic representation to ambassador level and restoring normal ties, the source stressed that it was too early to speak about this," KUNA said.
Jordan's Prime Minister Abdul-Karim al-Kabariti sent Kuwaiti Crown Prince Sheikh Saad al-Abdulla al-Sabah a message on his re-appointment this month as prime minister.
Sheikh Saad's response, KUNA said, was "a thank you message" which did not dwell on other issues.

Sheikh Saad in February also exchanged messages with his Jordanian counterpart, Crown Prince Hassan, in the first official contact between leading members of the states' ruling families since the 1990 Iraqi invasion of Kuwait.
A U.S.-led multinational force liberated Kuwait in 1991. The Gulf state downgraded diplomatic ties and cut off generous aid to several Arab states seen as Iraq supporters.

Relations with Jordan were at the centre of a row in December between Sheikh Saad, who has long opposed resuming ties with Jordan, and Foreign Minister Sheikh Sabah al-Ahmad al-Sabah, advocating a fence-mending approach.
Jordan's King Hussein, after distancing himself from Iraqi leader Saddam Hussein, has succeeded in improving ties with other Gulf Arab states including Saudi Arabia.
